correctness_confidence.basis: Checked by hand: Lemma 4, Lemma 5, Proposition 6 chain, parameter choice and arithmetic for (1) and (2), Corollaries 8-9, the Theorem 3 lower-bound algebra and Theorem 11 algebra. Section 6 (Theorem 2) is only sketched and was not verified.

rigor.basis: Theorems 1, 3 and 11 are argued in enough detail to follow and check. Theorem 2 depends on uniform derivative and global estimates that are asserted rather than shown, and Lemma 10 is a sketch. Explicit constants are given for (1) and (2).

novelty.basis: Theorem 1 sharpens Tan et al. (r_n >= exp(-(1+o(1)) sqrt(n) log n)) by removing the log factor, reusing their normalization and Newton identity with attribution. The 1/sqrt(8) circle-root limit and the one-interior-zero threshold are new relative to the cited work. Literature checked only via search snippets.

significance.basis: Settles the circle-root limit and the zero-count threshold for a narrow extremal residual problem. The negative answer to Erdos Problem 973 is credited to Luo-Yang-Zhu and Tan et al.; the exterior power-sum corollaries are quantitative refinements.

reproducibility.basis: Explicit circle-root family and one-root formulas are complete. Float64 recomputation matched the Theorem 3 family (squared restricted ratio 0.1255 at n=1200, k=0) and the Theorem 11 slope identity to six digits. Supplementary diagnostics and audit cited in Section 8 are not included.

summary: Polynomials of degree n with all zeros in the closed unit disk; residual rho(P) = ||P' - P'(0)P||_2 / ||P||_2 (unsquared). Claims: (i) for circle-root polynomials the least residual tends to 1/sqrt(8), via a Mathieu ground-state lower bound and an explicit family in every large degree; (ii) for disk-root polynomials and arbitrary slope, s_n >= exp(-C sqrt(n)) for C > sqrt((8/3) log 17), and s_n >= exp(-3 sqrt(n)) for n >= 10^4, with corollaries for exterior power sums; (iii) one interior zero permits rho = O(n^(-1/6)) by an explicit construction; (iv) for fixed A, a fixed number M_A of interior zeros permits O(n^(-A)), without effective constants. Checks: SHA-256 matched; full text read via pdftotext and page images; hand checks of Lemmas 4-5, Proposition 6, parameters for (1) and (2), Corollaries 8-9, the Theorem 3 lower-bound arithmetic (Mathieu expansion as recalled, not fetched) and the Theorem 11 algebra. Float64 checks: the circle-root family gives a squared restricted residual of 0.12548 at n=1200 (k=0); the one-root construction gives P'(0)=P'(1)/P(1) to six digits for n=35 to 1120, with squared residual falling from 0.673 (n=70) to 0.0596 (n=1120). Not verified: Section 6 proof of Theorem 2, Lemma 10, Section 8 supplementary diagnostics (not supplied), and literature beyond search snippets. Recommendation: major revision, mainly because the Theorem 2 proof cannot be checked from the text.
strengths: Theorem 1 proof chain checks: Lemma 4 normalization and separation, Lemma 5 Cauchy bound, the Proposition 6 Cesaro test, the choice giving C0 = sqrt((8/3) log 17), and the explicit arithmetic for n >= 10^4.

Theorem 3 upper bound is confirmed numerically: P'_{m,k}(0) = n/2 + 1/4 exactly, and the squared restricted residual tends to 1/8 (0.12548 at n=1200, k=0). The lower-bound expansion gives (c-1/4)^2 + 1/8 exactly, consistent with a_0(q) = -2q + 2 sqrt(q) - 1/4.

Theorem 11 explicit one-root family: identities (18)-(19), the slope and second-moment formulas, and the quadratic branch limit X -> 5/3, Y -> 1/4 check by hand. Numerically P'(0) = P'(1)/P(1) to six digits for n=35 to 1120.
Claims are scoped honestly: non-effective constants for Theorem 2, unresolved optimal rates, and explicit credit to Tan-Wang-Huang-Chen and Luo-Yang-Zhu.
weaknesses: Section 6 (Theorem 2) is a sketch. The outer-arc derivative bounds, the global estimate (16) and the Lemma 10 positivity argument are asserted in a line or two each, so the superalgebraic claim cannot be checked from the text.

Novelty over Tan et al. [1] is incremental: Theorem 1 keeps their maximum-point normalization and Newton identity and removes one log factor. The negative answer to Erdos Problem 973 is credited to prior work.

The residual convention changes between sections. The abstract and Theorem 3 use the unsquared ratio (limit 1/sqrt(8)), but the proofs of Theorem 3 and Section 6 work with squared quantities. The square-root step is not written out.

Supplementary diagnostics and the independent audit of all 34 degree classes (Section 8) are cited but not included, so they could not be checked. Numerically, the one-root squared residual decays faster than n^(-1/3) over n=560 to 1120, so the stated bound is not tight, which the paper does not claim.
potential_errors: Theorem 11 is stated as rho = O(n^(-1/6)), while its proof concludes rho^2 = O(n^(-1/3)). These are consistent, but the paper should state which exponent is the claim, and the abstract should match.
Section 2 gives the squared expansion (3) for the squared residual, and Theorem 3 is stated for the unsquared ratio. The passage from g_n to the limit 1/sqrt(8) needs an explicit square-root step.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact limit 1/sqrt(8) for the least normalized residual over circle-root polynomials, with an explicit family attaining it in every large degree (Theorem 3).
One interior zero suffices for a polynomial-rate residual, via an explicit algebraic construction, so one interior root is the minimal count for vanishing residual (Theorem 11).
unresolved_material_objections: Theorem 2 (superalgebraic upper bound with fixed M_A): Section 6 asserts uniform bounds without full estimates. These include the outer-arc derivative terms being polynomial in n times a Gaussian bound, the global estimate (16) with a uniform kappa, and the positivity of the weights from Lemma 10. Unless these are verified to be uniform in n for fixed K, the claim O(n^(-A)) with fixed M_A is unsupported. The reviewer could not check this from the text.
